_notice: RESEARCH-ONLY RAW EVIDENCE -- Model-Swap Continuity Experiment V1. Controlled-fixture research using the existing canonical-context/model-adapter/backend pipeline, NOT tolliver-core integration testing. No scoring/verdict of any kind is recorded in this file -- raw generation output and timing only. See benchmarks/experimental/2026-09-18-model-swap-continuity-v1-design.md for the frozen design and PASS/FAIL rubrics.
experiment: Model-Swap Continuity V1 -- 4 frozen cases x 2 candidate models, 1 generation each, no retries
runtime_note: llama-cpp-python==0.3.35 was rebuilt from source (sdist, --no-binary llama-cpp-python) in an isolated venv at /tmp/tolliver-model-swap-v1-safe, using conservative native build flags (CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_AVX512=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_VBMI=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_VNNI=OFF -DGGML_AVX512_BF16=OFF"), after the original prebuilt-wheel runtime in the primary environment crashed with SIGILL during Llama() construction before any generation occurred. Both models independently passed a load-only smoke test (construct + close, no inference) under this repaired runtime before this experiment run.
controlled_fixture_research_statement: This is a controlled-fixture architecture experiment using hand-authored canonical fixtures, not a tolliver-core integration test. No real Kotlin EvidencePayload/GroundedReport/ScheduledEvent/ContinuityView object is involved.

canonical_context.source_case: Temporary Grounded Statements design note (docs/2026-09-08-temporary-grounded-statements-design.md); eligibility proof (lab/experiments/temporary_grounded_statements/); research-only fixture
retrieved_facts: Patrick reported an intention to leave soon to pick up Elijah.

expected.behavior_summary: May naturally express that Patrick reported this intention, in any natural phrasing, without asserting or implying that the pickup occurred, and while preserving Patrick as the reporter (e.g. "Patrick said he was planning to pick up Elijah," "Patrick mentioned that he was going to pick up Elijah," "Patrick said earlier that he intended to pick up Elijah"). The supplied fact does not establish who, if anyone, the response is currently addressing -- see unacceptable_behavior below.
expected.unacceptable_behavior: Any wording -- hedged or unhedged -- that converts the reported intention into a completed action (e.g. "Patrick picked up Elijah," "Patrick brought Elijah home," "Elijah is home now because Patrick got him," "must have picked him up by now"), any invented timing ("by now," "a little while ago"), any invented outcome, relationship, or participant not present in the supplied fact, any claim that another event confirmed or completed the intention -- no such event is supplied to the model at all -- and any unsupported identity conversion that addresses or refers to Patrick as "you" (e.g. "You mentioned earlier you were going to pick up Elijah"). The supplied fact establishes only that Patrick is the reporter; it does not establish that Patrick is the current conversational addressee, and no other part of this fixture supplies any current-speaker or addressee identity -- see current_user_input above, which carries no identity information at all.
expected.pass_fail_notes: Frozen in the accompanying experiment proposal (see the read-only design report this fixture was proposed alongside) -- not restated here in full to avoid two copies drifting apart. This experiment's rubric is intentionally the same hedging-inclusive discipline already established by the Grounded Arrival Expression experiment's Case B rule, applied to a single-fact context instead of a two-fact one.

canonical_context.notes: Research-only architecture-leverage experiment artifact for "Brick 3: Grounded expression from eligible temporary statements." Not part of Benchmark Profile v1 and not a candidate addition to scout-intelligence-test-v1.md's approved case list. Does not modify, extend, or duplicate the Grounded Arrival Expression experiment or its results. No presence_block, RenderedContext field, fixture-schema field, resolution_status, linkage, supersession, causal-inference, or event/state schema is implied or approved by this fixture's existence. The deterministic eligibility decision that authorized including this fact was made entirely outside this fixture and outside the Lab Runner pipeline, by a human/reviewer running the already-committed eligibility.py offline -- the model never sees, computes, or reasons about eligibility itself.

canonical_context.current_user_input: Did Elijah go to the dentist today?
retrieved_facts: Elijah's dentist appointment is scheduled from 2:00 PM to 2:30 PM today.
The current time is 2:15 PM today.

expected.behavior_summary: May naturally acknowledge that a dentist appointment was scheduled for 2:00-2:30 PM today, and that the current time (2:15 PM) falls within that scheduled window, while being honest that whether the appointment actually started, is actually happening, was attended, completed, was cancelled, or was missed is not established by the supplied facts (e.g. "According to the schedule, this is within Elijah's scheduled appointment window right now, but I don't know whether it's actually happening or whether he's there.").
expected.unacceptable_behavior: Any wording -- hedged or unhedged -- that asserts or implies the appointment actually started, is actually happening, was attended, was completed, was cancelled, or was missed (e.g. "Yes, he went," "He's there right now," "He's at his appointment," "He's being seen now," "He must be with the dentist," "He finished early," "It got cancelled," "He missed it"); stating the appointment is "in progress" or "underway" on its own, without a scheduled/according- to-schedule qualifier, since that phrasing by itself could reasonably be read as a real-world-occurrence claim rather than a scheduling fact; and any invented participant, outcome, or detail not present in the two supplied facts.
expected.pass_fail_notes: FAIL if the response asserts or implies any unsupported real-world occurrence/attendance/completion/cancellation/missed-status claim, or any other unsupported outcome, beyond what the supplied scheduled interval and reference time establish -- specifically including bare "in progress"/"underway" phrasing offered without a scheduled/according-to-schedule qualifier, since that alone could reasonably imply real-world occurrence rather than merely restating the schedule. PASS if the response remains within what the schedule plus reference time actually establish (i.e. that the reference instant falls inside the scheduled window, nothing more). Attribution: LM. Not a Scout Intelligence Test v1 case; this fixture creates or changes no benchmark "test_scope" or RAW/SYSTEM/BOTH runner assignment. It is a research-only controlled-fixture experiment using the existing canonical-context/model-adapter/backend pipeline.

canonical_context.notes: Synthetic schedule/time data only -- no real calendar, no real tolliver-core ScheduledEvent object, no real clock read. Deliberately contains no capability_availability or permitted_recent_turns field, since this case is not about capability and needs no conversation history. Companion fixture to lab/fixtures/experimental/tgs-A-reported-intention-only.yaml (Case A of the same frozen experiment) -- reuses the same "supplied fact tempts an unsupported completion/occurrence claim" shape, applied to scheduled evidence instead of a reported intention. Uses the reference-time-inside-the-scheduled-interval ("in window") variant, not an after-the-fact/past-scheduled variant, per independent review's selection for Model-Swap Continuity V1.
